notes: EDA v4: reviewed findings, confidence and rule-input status are in reports/eda/SUMMARY.md and tools/scene/CONTRACT.md. The notes below are automatic descriptive statistics of this clip only.
1162 tracks in 318 s: 692 pedestrians (60%), 425 car, 17 bus, 22 truck, 6 motorcycle, 0 bicycle; 3 person boxes riding two-wheelers were relabelled as riders.
On average 26.7 pedestrians and 25 vehicles are on screen at once (peak 37 pedestrians).

4 vehicle flows found; the largest are F1 middle-right to top-left (right to left, 155 tracks); F2 top-left to bottom-right (towards camera, left to right, 151 tracks); F3 middle-left to bottom-left (towards camera, 8 tracks).

Furthest queued stop that began while head D showed red, red_amber or amber, per flow (rough upper bound for a stop line; D is a timing proxy for the near carriageway only): F1 near [1545, 472] (15% of its vehicles stopped >= 2 s, queue 1.2 vs 1.3 vehicles while D red vs not red); F2 near [3682, 2154] (53% of its vehicles stopped >= 2 s, queue 9.0 vs 3.3 vehicles while D red vs not red); F3 near [551, 980] (62% of its vehicles stopped >= 2 s, queue 0.8 vs 0.1 vehicles while D red vs not red).

Median pedestrian box height is 120 px at 4K; 27% are under 96px (16px at imgsz 640), 1% are under 64px (16px at imgsz 960), 0% are under 48px (16px at imgsz 1280). These are detected boxes, so the smallest people are already missing.

Mean luma goes from 94.1 to 94.4 (+0.4%) over the clip, range 91.1 to 99.6 of 255; the largest swing is +7.1% within 15 s (119 to 134 s). Iris, shutter and gain are constant in the camera metadata (reports/eda/camera), so this is not exposure control; brightness rules (fire_smoke) must still normalise per frame.

184 of 692 pedestrian tracks spend >= 0.5 s on cells used by moving vehicles; 5 crossing corridor(s) found, the busiest spans x 480 to 2320, y 960 to 1680 (107 people); 23 people are on the road outside corridors, most around [1578, 1436] (includes kerbside waiting and bus boarding, so an upper bound for jaywalking).

Signal: vehicle head D (3 lamps, from the head inventory) at (2315, 773) in this video; its v4 timeline has a known state for 99.4% of the clip (coverage, not accuracy: no human-verified labels yet). D is a timing proxy for the near-carriageway flow; which movements it controls is unknown.

Of 330 vehicle tracks with enough motion, 272 go straight, 44 turn and 8 reverse heading (U-turn like, e.g. track 21 at [3165, 1268] around 27.3 s); check these by eye before treating them as illegal_u_turn examples.
4 vehicle(s) stand still for over 90% of a track longer than 60 s at [176, 1053], [134, 909], [59, 816], [3703, 938] (parked), which a stopped_vehicle rule must whitelist or time-gate.
Tracker: 19.1% of tracks live under 1 s and 69.8% of vehicle tracks start away from the frame edge, a sign of occlusion and ID switches.

lane_flow_clustering.method: k-means on start xy, end xy, net heading, then merge clusters that share heading (< 20 deg) and line (< 250 px)
lane_flow_clustering.rule: vehicle tracks >= 2 s and >= 300 px net travel

turning_movements.rule: heading change between first and last 5 moving samples; |d| < 35 straight, > 140 U-turn like; image-plane, so perspective bends it

signal.status: PROVISIONAL (coverage only; no human-verified lamp labels yet)
signal.box_mapping: box_ref (reference C3897 4K px) mapped with H_ref_to_video from registration.json
signal.meaning: head D is a strong timing proxy for the near-carriageway flow; the far carriageway is also cycle-locked with a different phase offset; which movements D physically controls is UNKNOWN (reports/eda/SUMMARY.md, finding 3)

perspective.assumption: person height about 1.7 m; valid only near the fitted y range

pedestrians_on_carriageway.definition: person ground point in a direction-field cell used by moving vehicles, >= 5 samples (~0.5 s)
pedestrians_on_carriageway.corridor_rule: road cells with >= 10 distinct people, dilated by one cell
